solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Refuse-collector maybe has turned writer

indicators.note: turned means the letters of has, with the writer's word, are turned about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a nib is the writing point of a pen, so it stands for a writer

explanation.surface: Someone who collects rubbish has, perhaps, become an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse-collector' suggests a dustman; 'maybe' marks the bin as one example of something that collects refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustbin for ashes and rubbish collects refuse, hence 'maybe' marking it as an example.

clue.text: Missionary who can handle a spoon?

definitions.text: Missionary who can handle a spoon?

parts.words: Missionary who can handle a spoon?
parts.note: ... spoons have handles topped with figures of the disciples

explanation.walkthrough: Apostle spoons are old silver spoons whose handles end in a figure of one of Christ's disciples.
explanation.definitionFit: The disciples sent out by Christ were missionaries, and their figures form spoon handles.

clue.text: People are known to hit them

definitions.text: People are known to hit them

parts.words: People are known to hit them
parts.note: the idiom 'hit the ...' means become newsworthy, not strike anything

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who becomes famous or notorious is said to hit the front-page banners of newspapers.

clue.text: I shall employ abuse

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I shall
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: Someone declares an intention to put mistreatment to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To ill-use someone is to treat them badly, mistreat or misuse them.

clue.text: Acclamation of unusual papal custom

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of papal set in a different, odd order

parts.note: a custom or habit is a use, as in 'usage'

explanation.surface: Cheering greets a strange habit of the pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapping is the noise of public praise, so it is a form of acclaim.

clue.text: Vessel for runner-up in race

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: the runner-up comes second, so this picks the second letter of the word race

explanation.surface: A boat built for the crew that finished second in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner-up' looks like a second-placed competitor; it picks the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A proa is a Malay or Pacific sailing boat with an outrigger, a kind of craft.

clue.text: Reluctant to have a port with a philanderer

parts.note: loth (also loath) means unwilling
Rio de Janeiro is a port, often just Rio

explanation.surface: Unwilling to take a harbour along with a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, a seducer in an old play, became a byword for a man who toys with women's affections.

clue.text: Vessel about to be broken up

indicators.note: broken up means the letters of about are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A ship is about to be scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated form is a German submarine of the world wars.
explanation.definitionFit: A German submarine is a vessel, named from the German Unterseeboot.

clue.text: Green organisation after record stand

indicators.note: after places the reshuffled letters following the record

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: organisation suggests the letters of Green are organised into a new order

explanation.surface: An environmental group is formed after a disc is released and stands firm.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is an ornamental centrepiece for a dining table, a tiered stand for fruit or flowers.

clue.text: Nothing clear may come from this prophet

parts.note: nothing is zero, the round letter O

indicators.note: may come from suggests the letters of clear can be reshaped to produce something new

explanation.surface: A seer from whom nothing plain can be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jokes that this prophet's sayings are never clear, as the Delphic ones were famously ambiguous.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle was a person or shrine through which a god foretold the future, much like a seer.

clue.text: Shelve mail — perhaps open later

indicators.note: later places the reshuffled word after the first piece

parts.note: mail and post both mean letters sent

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters of open are only one possible arrangement

explanation.surface: Put the letters aside and maybe open them another time.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelve a plan is to put it off until another time, i.e. delay it.

clue.text: Dud cheque chucker-out

definitions.meaning: a cheque that the bank returns unpaid, figuratively springing back
a doorman who throws troublemakers out of a club

explanation.definitionFit: A rubber cheque that 'bounces' and a nightclub doorman both share this one noun.

clue.text: Gossips at dance discuss business

parts.note: one who gossips talks, chattering about others
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: People chattering at a dance end up discussing their work.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'talk shop' means to discuss one's work or trade, often in a social setting.

clue.text: Student's carnival game for the common people

parts.note: a rag is a British students' charity carnival or fundraising week
tag is the children's chasing game

explanation.surface: A university fundraising event's game is laid on for ordinary folk.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG week is a British university tradition of charity stunts and parades.
explanation.definitionFit: The ragtag, as in 'ragtag and bobtail', is a dismissive term for the rabble or lower orders.

clue.text: Girl I sign on as an astronomer

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A young woman signs me up as a stargazer.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian scientist who studied the heavens through his telescope.

clue.text: Stake for backing hotly-tipped runner

indicators.note: backing means the stake word is read from back to front

parts.note: an ante is a poker player's stake placed before the deal

explanation.surface: A bet supporting a racehorse that the experts fancy.
explanation.walkthrough: The racing surface makes 'hotly-tipped runner' look like a favourite; it is a volcano with a fiery top whose lava runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Etna is a volcano whose summit is hot and whose molten lava runs down its slopes.

clue.text: Never satisfied with played out banalities

indicators.note: played out suggests the letters of banalities are worked through into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone always restless with tired clichés.
explanation.definitionFit: Insatiable describes an appetite or desire that can never be filled or appeased.

clue.text: Changes mind in club game

indicators.note: in places the altered letters inside the club word

parts.note: a baton is a short stick or club

indicators.note: Changes signals that the letters of mind are altered in order

explanation.surface: Someone has second thoughts about a sport at the club.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: Like the fare if it's too high?

definitions.text: Like the fare if it's too high?

parts.words: Like the fare if it's too high?
parts.note: fare looks like a ticket price, but means food; meat gone high is rotten

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a travel price that is too dear; here it is food, and 'high' meat is going off.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off cannot be eaten, the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Madrid is in her itinerary, but part can be cut off

indicators.note: part signals that only a run of letters from the travel phrase is used

explanation.surface: A Spanish city appears on her travel plan, but some section may be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone off, in the will sense, is to deprive them of an inheritance.

clue.text: She robbed her sleeping partner of his capital assets

definitions.text: She robbed her sleeping partner of his capital assets

parts.words: She robbed her sleeping partner of his capital assets
parts.note: capital assets sounds financial, but means the hair on Samson's head, cut while he slept

explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible Delilah had Samson's hair cut as he slept, taking his strength; 'capital' puns on head, 'sleeping partner' on business.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical temptress betrayed Samson by shearing his hair, the source of his strength.

clue.text: A cheese that's made round

indicators.note: round means the word made is turned about, read in reverse

explanation.surface: A cheese produced in a round shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Edam is famously made as a round ball, so 'round' looks descriptive in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a Dutch cheese, typically sold in balls with a red wax coat.

clue.text: Not a subject put on in advance

indicators.note: put in means the small word goes inside the advance word

parts.note: to march is to advance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A topic is not being added to the march forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A king or queen rules over subjects rather than being one, so a sovereign is no subject.

clue.text: A gunsmith will add it to his stock

definitions.text: A gunsmith will add it to his stock

parts.words: A gunsmith will add it to his stock
parts.note: stock reads as goods on hand, but is the wooden butt of a gun to which the tube is fitted

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like inventory; on a gun it is the shoulder piece, and the tube fitted to it is the barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's tube, through which the shot passes, is fixed to the wooden stock.

clue.text: Snobbish boy and girl

parts.note: a lad is a boy
Ida is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young couple who are rather stuck-up.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes affected, pretentious manners, the speech of someone putting on airs.

clue.text: Grand old man longing to give party support

indicators.note: support in a down clue puts the longing word beneath the party word

parts.note: a do is a party
a yen is a yearning or longing

explanation.surface: A distinguished elder wishes to back a political group.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the senior, most respected member of a group or profession.

clue.text: Rex — Joy's brother perhaps

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king
elation is great joy

explanation.surface: A man named Rex is the brother of a woman called Joy.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex and Joy read as names; Rex gives R, as in the regnal 'ER', and joy is a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother is one example of a relative, a kinsman by family ties.

clue.text: Victor, say, to embrace with love

parts.note: to hug someone is to embrace them
love is nil in tennis, the round letter O

explanation.surface: Victor is invited to hold someone tenderly.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor is the first name of Victor Hugo, the French novelist; 'say' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor is a first name; the French author Victor Hugo shows his surname matches it.

clue.text: Attack a lazy fellow

definitions.meaning: to ... someone is to hit out at them on all sides

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb 'lay about' means assail, and as one noun it names a shiftless loafer.

clue.text: Depression after an attack, perhaps

parts.note: reads as low mood after a medical or verbal attack, but means a pit in the ground left by a bomb

explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' tempts towards gloom; the attack is a bombing, leaving a hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb or shell blasts a bowl-shaped hole in the ground, a hollow depression.

clue.text: A dependant — one who keeps going

definitions.meaning: someone who attaches themselves to another for support or favour
read literally, one who holds on and persists

explanation.definitionFit: A sycophantic follower clings on to a patron, and 'hang on' also means persevere.

clue.text: But it's not how boxers settle matters

definitions.text: But it's not how boxers settle matters

parts.words: But it's not how boxers settle matters
parts.note: the word means settle a deal, yet in boxing it names holding the opponent, which decides nothing

explanation.walkthrough: In boxing, a clinch is when fighters grab hold of each other to rest; elsewhere the word means to settle or seal a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to settle decisively, while the boxers' hold of that name settles nothing.
